tools.name: atlas
tools.tagline: Segment Atlas, the same numbers for every published segment
tools.summary: `python -m kit atlas` measures every tifxyz mesh on the open-data bucket with [`kit tifxyz`](tifxyz.md)'s checks and publishes one table, the daily-refreshed dataset [SharpMeow/vesuvius-segment-atlas](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/vesuvius-segment-atlas).

go_ahead.text: Not needed for `build` and `show` (public data, local files). The dataset is public, published after the leak check (AGENTS.md rule 8; Chase asked for it on 24 Oct 2026)

tools.license: Code Apache-2.0; the dataset's numbers and preview grids CC BY-NC 4.0, as the meshes they come from (Vesuvius Challenge open data, CC BY-NC 4.0)

fields.Kind: kit command, kit module, script, data
fields.Run: `python -m kit atlas build`, `python -m kit atlas show`, `python -m kit.atlas`, `from kit import atlas`, `python scripts/atlas/hf_atlas.py`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy and tifffile (imagecodecs for the LZW-compressed meshes, about a fifth of them); scipy when installed. `huggingface_hub` only for `scripts/atlas/hf_atlas.py`
fields.Runs on: Any CPU, but the whole bucket is large: 908 meshes, 69.4 GB of x, y and z files (listed 24 Oct 2026), 50.6 GB of them PHerc. Paris 4's. Per mesh on a 4-core cloud container (24 Oct 2026, download included): 1.2 to 1.5 s at 9.362 um, 7.6 to 8.4 s at 2.4 um, 23.5 s at 1.129 um. The largest mesh (about 116 million nodes) needs about 3 GB of memory, so the daily build runs as a Hugging Face Job on `cpu-upgrade` (8 vCPU, 32 GB)
fields.Network: `vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` (metadata.json, ListObjectsV2 listings, each mesh's four files); `show` reads the published `atlas.jsonl` from `huggingface.co` unless `--atlas` names a file
fields.Writes: `build`: OUT/`atlas.jsonl`, `atlas.csv`, `summary.json`, `README.md` and, with `--lens`, `lens/*.slg.gz`; each mesh is fetched into a temporary folder that is deleted after it is measured. `show`: nothing. `hf_atlas.py job`: the public dataset
fields.License: Code Apache-2.0; the dataset's numbers and preview grids CC BY-NC 4.0, as the meshes they come from (Vesuvius Challenge open data, CC BY-NC 4.0)
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed for `build` and `show` (public data, local files). The dataset is public, published after the leak check (AGENTS.md rule 8; Chase asked for it on 24 Oct 2026)
fields.Released: Public `main` from the change that adds it (24 Oct 2026)

tools.name: auc
tools.tagline: score an ink map against a segment's published labels
tools.summary: `python -m kit auc` gives the pixel AUC of a 2D ink map against a segment's `inklabels.zarr` inside its `supervision.zarr`, with the reverse-depth map as the control, block-bootstrap intervals, and a paired test of whether one map beats another.

go_ahead.text: Not needed

fields.Run: `python -m kit auc`, `from kit import auc`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, tifffile (imagecodecs for LZW or zstd TIFFs), zarr (3.x on Python 3.11 or newer; 2.x works for reading)
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A full-size 5,980 x 8,240 map takes about 5 s with a control and about 6 s with `--bootstrap 300` (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core 2.1 GHz Xeon cloud container, synthetic data)
fields.Network: None
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). With `--slug SLUG`, appends one check to `experiments/SLUG/run.json` (or `ROOT/SLUG/run.json` with `--root`)
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07; also inside the AutoPipeline release

tools.name: autopipeline
tools.tagline: run villa's pipeline from a released scan to a scored ink map, unattended
tools.summary: AutoPipeline (AP) 0.1.7 runs villa's VC3D tools and ink detection on one released scan, from its headers to checked surfaces, ink maps with reversed and shuffled controls, and scores; its code is on public branch `submission/progress-2026-10-fix7`, not on `main`.

go_ahead.text: Needed for a paid batch or any cloud (Modal) launch, which costs money (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8); not needed for the demo, `defaults`, `plan` or a local run

tools.license: Code: Apache License 2.0 ([LICENSE on the branch](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/24572e6203bafa67de1611bcd31b9edebe2c078e/submissions/progress-2026-10-fix7/autopipeline/LICENSE)); data and model weights keep their own licenses and are not included

fields.Code: `submissions/progress-2026-10-fix7/autopipeline/` on its branch: mainly `kit/autopipe.py` (`cmd_autopipe`, `build_parser`, `DEFAULTS`), `kit/autopipe_monitor.py`, `kit/apconsole.py` (the console), `kit/qareasons.py`, `kit/apbackends.py`, `kit/vc3d_agent.py`, `kit/vc3d_cache.py`, `kit/cli.py`, `scripts/demo_synthetic.py`, `scripts/get_vc3d.py`, `scripts/vc3d/ink.py`; release record `submissions/progress-2026-10-fix7/release.json`
fields.Tests: `submissions/progress-2026-10-fix7/autopipeline/tests/` on its branch: 46 `test_*.py` files, among them `test_autopipe.py` (the whole chain on a synthetic scroll with stand-in VC3D tools), `test_autopipe_monitor.py`, `test_autopipe_monitor_ui.py` (the monitor page in a local Chromium), `test_demo_synthetic.py` and `test_vc3d_agent.py`, with stand-in tools in `vc3d_fakes.py`
fields.Needs: Python 3.11 or newer (zarr 3 needs it); numpy, tifffile, zarr 3 and scipy (`pyproject.toml`, tested 2026-10-12 with numpy 2.4.6, tifffile 2026.3.3, zarr 3.1.6, scipy 1.17.1). For real runs: villa's VC3D tools (`vc_gen_umbilicus`, `vc_grow_seg_from_seed`, `vc_tifxyz_selfcross`, `vc_flatten`, `vc_render_tifxyz`), from villa's Linux x86_64 AppImage or `VC3D.app` on a Mac; for ink, villa's `vesuvius` package and torch in their own environment (`KIT_INK_PYTHON`). Optional, for the browser tests only: the `playwright` Python package and a system `chromium` or `chromium-browser`; without them those tests skip and download nothing
fields.Runs on: The synthetic demo: 13.1 s as it reports itself in a cloud container, Python 3.13, from the 0.1.7 package's release check (2026-10-24; it now draws a CT with planted strokes); the package's 1249 tests took 506 s there (35 skipped, 8 of them the Chromium page tests, which passed in a second run with Chromium on the path). With 0.1.6 the demo reported 5.5 s. With 0.1.5 it reported 4.7 s on a shared 4-core container (2026-10-18). A real run on PHerc0841 w00 from the released scan and published segment: 593 s, 344 s on 8 CPU cores then 249 s on one L4, on Modal (package README, 9 October 2026); the three-reader rerun took 1163 s on 8 CPU cores and one L4 (package README, 15 October 2026). GPU ink runs on Hugging Face (hard rule 11)

The monitor listens on `127.0.0.1` only and loads nothing from the internet. The synthetic demo needs no network
fields.Writes: A run folder `work/autopipe/<sample>-<volume>-<digest10>/` under the kit home (the package folder, or `KIT_HOME`): `plan.json`, `state.json`, `events.jsonl`, traces, renders, ink maps, `scores.json`, `report.json` and, when ink is handed off, `modal-job.json`; `work/vc3d/` for the catalog cache and the unpacked AppImage (about 370 MB). The demo writes to a temporary folder under `/tmp` and prints its path. `monitor --snapshot FILE.html` writes one HTML file
fields.Go-ahead: Needed for a paid batch or any cloud (Modal) launch, which costs money (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8); not needed for the demo, `defaults`, `plan` or a local run
fields.Released: Public branch `submission/progress-2026-10-fix7` at `24572e6` (committed 2026-10-24, a commit with no parent; README entry dated 2026-10-24 in [`releases.json`](../releases.json), pinned to the top of "Released tools"). tools.name: axispolish
tools.tagline: polish a center line to the deepest point of the traced sheet
tools.summary: `python -m kit axispolish` moves a scroll's center line (umbilicus), slice by slice, to the point of highest winding coverage nearby on the scan's published normal grids, and writes it back in the published format for VC3D and the spiral fit.

go_ahead.text: Not needed: local arithmetic on public grids

fields.Run: `python -m kit axispolish`, `from kit import axispolish`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer and numpy; numba optional (the same sums compiled, about 8 times faster); the scan's level-0 normal grids, found on the open-data bucket or given with `--grids`
fields.Runs on: CPU. About 1.4 s per slice with numba on 4 cloud cores (PHerc0175A, 91 slices in 127 s with grids cached, 24 Oct 2026); about 6 s per slice with numpy alone (the frozen test's development runs, 22 Oct 2026); a whole line is about 100 slices, see Cost and time
fields.Network: `vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`: one bucket listing to find the grids, then one `xy/NNNNNN.grid` file per polished slice. None with a local `--grids` folder
fields.Writes: The polished line at `--out` (parent folders created); with `--cache DIR`, the downloaded grid files under `DIR/xy/`
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed: local arithmetic on public grids
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-24; a line of the Scrolls kit entry in the README's "Released tools"

tools.name: batch
tools.tagline: plan, price and queue AutoPipeline over every scan in the open-data bucket
tools.summary: `python -m kit run catalog`, `run all` and `run watch` list every volume of the Vesuvius Challenge open-data bucket, give each one an AutoPipeline config and a Modal price, and queue them in a resumable, approvable dry-run plan; they never launch anything.

go_ahead.text: Not needed for `catalog`, `watch`, `--dry-run` or `--status`: they launch, post and spend nothing. Needed for `--approve`: run it only with the digest Chase approved, and each approved scan's Modal launch needs his yes and budget (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)

fields.Run: `python -m kit run all`, `python -m kit run watch`, `python -m kit run catalog`, `from kit import autobatch, scancatalog`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. Reads `kit/data/modal-rates.json` (through [cloudcost](cloudcost.md)) and the prizes snapshot `kit/data/prizes-2026-10-11.json`. Launching an approved scan needs the released AutoPipeline package (`scrolls-kit`), which this tool does not call
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A dry run of a 5-volume synthetic catalog took 0.19 s (measured 2026-10-16, cloud container). A catalog of the real bucket: Not measured; it is a few hundred small HTTPS requests
fields.Network: `run catalog`, `run watch`, and `run all` with `--refresh` or with no saved catalog: anonymous HTTPS GETs of `https://vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.amazonaws.com/metadata.json`, the bucket's S3 listing (root and each `SAMPLE/volumes/`) and `https://scrollprize.org/prizes` (skipped by `run catalog --no-live-prizes`). `run all` and `run watch` also GET each in-bucket volume's `.zattrs`, and `0/.zarray` when the shape is missing, once (cached). `dl.ash2txt.org` is refused. Nothing is posted
fields.Writes: `run catalog`: `--out` only (default `work/autobatch/catalog.json`). `run all` and `run watch`: under `--state` (default `work/autobatch/`, git-ignored): `catalog.json`, `plan.json`, `plan.md`, `batch-ledger.csv`, `approval.json`, `scans/SAMPLE/VOLUME/status.json` and `settings.json`, `zattrs/` caches. `run all --status` writes nothing
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed for `catalog`, `watch`, `--dry-run` or `--status`: they launch, post and spend nothing. Needed for `--approve`: run it only with the digest Chase approved, and each approved scan's Modal launch needs his yes and budget (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-16 ([PR #93](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/93))
fields.Guide: [AutoPipeline reference, section 19](../autopipeline/README.md#19-every-scan-catalog-batch-and-watcher)

tools.tagline: see which wraps and heights of a scroll the published segments trace, and where the gaps are

fields.Needs: Python 3.9 or newer, numpy, tifffile (imagecodecs for LZW-compressed meshes); Pillow only for `scripts/media/coverage_still.py`. A public center line for the volume, or your own with `--line`

tools.name: cropscan
tools.tagline: pixel AUC of one ink map on every window of a grid

go_ahead.text: Not needed

fields.Run: None (library): `from kit import cropscan`, then `cropscan.scan(...)`

fields.Go-ahead: Not needed

tools.name: crowdmerge
tools.tagline: fuse several traces of one sheet into one surface and flag each trace's slips
tools.summary: `python -m kit crowdmerge merge` fuses several tifxyz traces of the same papyrus sheet into one consensus surface by a vote along the surface normal, and flags where each trace slid onto a neighboring sheet; `bench` scores it on planted slips in PHerc0139's hand-traced windings.

go_ahead.text: Not needed: local CPU, your own traces or public data

fields.Run: `python -m kit crowdmerge merge`, `python -m kit crowdmerge bench`, `from kit import crowdmerge`; the real-crowd test: `python scripts/crowdmerge/realcrowd.py seeds|score`

fields.Go-ahead: Not needed: local CPU, your own traces or public data

tools.name: windlabel-box
tools.tagline: relative windings in a box, from published predictions
tools.summary: `python -m kit windlabel-box` grows chains of sheet crossings around a point on a published surface prediction, cuts them where lasagna's grad_mag sees more than one sheet, and writes villa's `relative_windings.json` for a spiral fit; a VC3D plugin runs it at the focus point.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run it: it reads published predictions and writes local files. Output from prize-eligible scrolls stays private until the prize announcement

fields.Run: `python -m kit windlabel-box`, `python3 plugins/run_kit.py windlabel-box` (the VC3D plugin `plugins/scrolls-windlabel-box.json`), `from kit import windlabel_box`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy and scipy; numcodecs for blosc-compressed zarrs such as the open-data m7; a published binary surface prediction at level 0 (such as the organizers' m7) and the same scroll's published lasagna grad_mag; the scroll's umbilicus in the prediction's level-0 voxels. The plugin needs VC3D with the Plugins menu (villa branch `vc3d-plugins`, not yet in villa main) and an attached umbilicus
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. Synthetic spiral (240 x 240 x 48 voxels, 30 seeds): about 1 s. PHerc0139 over HTTPS from the open-data bucket: 13 s for a 512 voxel box with 200 seeds, about 25 s with 1,000 seeds (18 boxes in 7 min 34 s; measured 2026-10-24, 4-core cloud container)
fields.Network: Reads the prediction, the grad_mag and a `*.lasagna.json` manifest over HTTPS when given URLs, such as `vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` (anonymous); nothing with local zarrs
fields.Writes: In `--out` (created): `chains.json`, `features.json`, `split.json`, `relative_windings.json`, `flags.json`, `export.json`. VC3D runs it in `~/.vc3d/plugin-runs/scrolls.windlabel-box/TIME/` and adds the windings as point collections
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run it: it reads published predictions and writes local files. Output from prize-eligible scrolls stays private until the prize announcement
fields.Released: Public `main` from the merge of its pull request (prepared 24 Oct 2026); a line of the Scrolls kit entry in the README's "Released tools", id `windlabel-box`

tools.tagline: the pip-installable scrolls-workbench package and the CI that tests it
tools.summary: `pyproject.toml` makes this repository's `kit` folder an installable package, `scrolls-workbench`, with three extras and five console scripts; `.github/workflows/check.yml` tests it on every push and pull request, and `CITATION.cff` says how to cite it.

fields.Run: `python -m pip install "scrolls-workbench[reader] @ git+https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls"`, then `scrolls-workbench`, `scrolls-letterread`, `scrolls-letterlines`, `scrolls-letterdemo`, `scrolls-start`, `import kit`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer (`requires-python = ">=3.10"`); pip with network access to fetch `setuptools>=77` for the build. The core needs no other package; the extras add numpy, pillow, tifffile, imagecodecs, zarr 3 (Python 3.11 or newer only) and scipy
fields.Runs on: Linux, macOS and Windows (the CI's reader job runs all three). Installing with no extras from a local copy took about 6 s (measured 2026-10-16, cloud container, Python 3.13)
